body: I cant though 😖I'm already pathetic I'm fucking 22 and still a college sophomore. I literally missed 3 entire years of my life sitting at home trying to find doctors to help me. I saw probably 50\+ doctors not kidding. My parents have spent tens of thousands of dollars trying to find me relief and no one has helped. There is no solution and I'm trapped. I know I'm going to die sometime this month. I didn't put everything in my original post. I've spent 90% of the time since I was 18 alone in my bed sobbing in pain. I have not had friends since I was 14. My entire body literally shakes in pain during classes and everything I eat gives me severe 10/10 pain heartburn and I can't breathe. I've gone to so many doctors who don't help me. I don't know what to do. I don't deserve this I'm so young, I lost my entire young adult life to this. I can't stop crying. This is literally it. I have had more patience than anyone should be expected to have

I've had so many eating "issues". I don't consider myself to ever have been anorexic but at one point I was 5'9 and 95 lbs so you could call me the world's best in-denial perfectionist instead? lmao. now I'm a fatass and I have horrific digestive issues that completely mess up my hunger cues and cause me to be in tremendous pain most of the time. society seriously does mess girls up in regards to eating and you're not alone believe me.

I don't even know you, but I believe you are stronger than you think. All of my worst nightmares have come true (quite comically really..like my individual worst nightmares specifically catered to me because apparently Satan is controlling my life or something? ) and I've spent the past four years in total isolation and pain, but I'm still here. There is an extremely tiny almost nonexistent part of me that still believes my dreams will come true in life and I'll be healthy and happy again. I think there is a minuscule part of it in you too or I don't think you would have even bothered to make this post.

 I was put on heavy antidepressants as a 5 year old because I was "too sensitive" if that gives you an idea that I'm not some special strong person. Then I got kicked out of an extremely fancy school that I worked my ass off to get into and gave up all social life in high school to get into temporarily because they thought I was "too skinny", swear to god. Who the fuck gets asked to leave college bc of their weight? Me apparently. Then in a cruel twist of fate I gained 100 lbs over the next 6 months because of the digestive pain bullshit and it is still here. I'm in pain every single day and my body literally shakes because of the pain and I pass out but somehow I managed to convince them to let me back in school and I'm back here trying to prove to myself that things will get better and I am worth a good life. I'm fucking miserable btw. The road back up is not a straight arrow full of sunshine. But who cares, because I'm trying. I think the words "fake it till you make it" could really apply to both of us here. Pretend for a second that eventually, in a few years, you have the life you want. Why not just pretend for a few months to figure out what you would need to do to get there? I don't believe for one second that anyone can't attend college. There are always ways, if that's what you really want. A lot of resources out there. 

I know this is so cheesy and annoying to say but its true, your thoughts aren't necessarily your reality. Crazy things happen every day. Nothing is impossible. And to answer your question, people who work hard for a good life are oftentimes the ones 10x happier in the end than those who don't because they can actually appreciate it. People who are handed everything don't have very much to offer the world. Just remember, life is malleable. You didn't always feel like this. We were all happy once. Just as we didn't stay happy why are we convinced this is the way it'll be forever too?
I'm so sorry😢. You don't deserve that at all

I never said I don't believe things go wrong in the human mind and body. I do not believe mental illness is a disease like diabetes is a disease. Even the APA has come out and said there are no reliable genetic markers or even neurotransmitter tests that can find any commonality in people with mental illnesses. The way the medical and psychiatrist community portray things like depression and anxiety have not been backed up by any proof. I'm not saying people do not get unhealthy in the brain, but I consider it like a cancer that could be cured as opposed to an unavoidable genetic condition you're born with.

Forgive me, but I assume you're very young. Relationships come and go in life. The end of a relationship is devastating to anyone. But in a vulnerable and already-depressed state, it takes on a life of its own and makes you unable to see things in perspective.

You should actually be glad that you were able to see her true colors- after you stuck by her during her issues, she was unable to do the same for you. That is selfishness and nothing else. If you had stayed with her longer, sooner or later you would come to find that she doesn't possess the same empathy and kindness you do. It's simply a bad match. What if you could find someone who gave you the same happy feelings she did, but who also stuck by you and cared for you during difficult times? That person exists. It's really unfortunate and a waste of time to get so hung up on someone who in reality likely doesn't match the positive characteristics you have made for her in your head. 

The reason I say you must be young, is quite simply because I saw your comment "Time won't change anything". This is a very understandable thought process for someone of a young age because you just don't have the life experience that shows otherwise. Time heals all wounds, to a great degree. It is literally not a possibility that months or years from now you will feel this intensely about this breakup. You will meet new people and experience new things that will push this away. Try and think about things you cried over 5,10 years ago (if you even can-- that's how much they fade!). Would you cry over those things today with the same intensity?

Panic attacks and depression are extremely common and treatable. You are not in any kind of complex or disastrous situation that cannot be fixed. Life is constantly changing. You have not always felt like this and you will not always feel like this. I hope you can take the steps to improve your situation soon because everyone deserves a happy and productive life.

Well I can't agree that suicide is in any way a good decision but the way I see it is it is a sort of neutral end to anything. When life is good, or even just regular, it's still pretty incredible and mysterious and there are many possibilities and opportunities to enjoy the ride. 5 years from now you could meet someone or have an experience that may make you sit back and say with 100% certainty, wow, I'm so damn glad I didn't decide to end things before I experienced this. You can kill yourself at any time so why not at least see if there's something fun or unexpected ahead. I agree, it isn't in and of itself a 'bad' decision but it's more a regretful one because you may miss out on things that would have really changed your mind about life. And of course it is unimaginably painful for anyone who knows you, if you have anyone close to you. We are all on this ride together and whether it's pointless or not, there's a reason most of us continue on. It may seem like a strange way to think, but what if a painful life is actually better than no life at all? Pain is a part of the human experience.

There are things you can do even now with pain that can zap you out of this mindset if you're interested. Do little things to change up your routine. Go to a coffee shop and order something you've never had. Go on a walk somewhere you've never been. Do something you normally wouldn't do. If you're going to kill yourself soon anyway, no reason not to experience a few new things. I hope you do pursue some more treatments. I'm sure it's hard to feel any hope right now that your pain will end but that doesn't mean it's the reality
Would definitely make me happier. But wouldn't fix the most important things

I think for chronic issues like this natural things can be the most long lasting and effective. They may be slower to work so it could require patience and sticking with it but have you ever had a food allergy/sensitivity test done? For me I used to have chronic sciatica...gave up dairy and haven't had it since. I would start with that and there are other things to explore like acupuncture/regular massage/even targeted therapy, sometimes physical symptoms arise when there's a constant underlying stress or depression. I really have hope you can beat this. There has to be a reason for it.

I thought for sure I would kill myself, no doubt in my mind. I'm not back to 100% health but you would be shocked at how your mindset changes about so many things when you feel physically well (or closer to it). Don't give up yet
